text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL TELECOM CONCESSION FEES TO BE PAID IN CASH
Brazil's new telecommunications law would require firms holding concessions to operate telecoms services would pay concession fees in cash, according to a bill sent to Congress Thursday.
-- BRAZIL'S FIPE POSTS FIRST DEFLATION SINCE 1957
Consumer prices as measured by Brazil's Economic Research Institute (Fipe) fell 0.03 percent in the four weeks ending December 8, Fipe's first report of deflation in Brazil since 1957.
-- THREE CONSORTIA AIM TO BID ON SOUTH BRANCH RAILWAY
Three consortia intend to bid on a concession to run the South Branch of Brazil's federal railway network, which is slated to go on the auction block today at Rio de Janeiro's stock market.
O GLOBO
-- PRESIDENT APOLOGIZES TO COURT FOR MINISTER'S INTERFERENCE

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso apologized yesterday for Administration Minister Bresser Pereira's cricism of Supreme Federal Tribunal President Sepulveda Pertence, calling the minister's interference in court matters a "national disaster."
-- GASOLINE AND GASOHOL PRICES TO RISE ON TUESDAY
Fuel prices will rise on Tuesday, with gasoline and gasohol climbing between 8 percent and 10.5 percent while deisel rises 9.7 percent in Rio de Janeiro state.
-- DEAL REACHED ROR ROMARIO TO RETURN TO SPAIN

A deal has been reached for Brazilian football star Romario to return toplay on Spain's Valencia, but there's one snag: Romario wants to stay in Brazil until his contract with home team Flamengo expires in July.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- FUEL TO RISE UP TO 10.2 PERCENT ON TUESDAY

Gasoline and gasohol prices will rise on Tuesday, in areas such as Sao Paulo state where prices are free-floating by as much as 10.2 percent and in the north and northeast of Brazil where prices are controlled by as much as 22.3 percent.
-- CONGRESS BUDGET PANEL RELATOR MAY BE INVESTIGATED

Congress's lower house approved a report calling for the cassation of a deputy at the heart of a budget fraud scandal and asking Congress to probe the senator who is relator of its joint budget commission.
-- SAO PAULO HAS DEFLATION FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE 1957
Sao Paulo has posted its first deflation in the ofur-week paeriod ending December 8, with prices falling 0.03 percent, according to the Fipe economic studies institute.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
